comparison: Both strongly support the activity-guided fractionation methodology and discovery of lysophospholipids as pannexin activators (C3, C24-C27). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of convergent experimental approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'elegant approach.' OpenEval also includes C31, C32, C34 which peer reviewers address separately in R2.

Both support the structure-activity relationship findings for different LPC types (C38-C43). OpenEval emphasizes systematic testing with dose-response curves and physiological relevance inference. Peer reviewers explicitly noted the 'robust methodologies' for evaluating 'many different types of LPCs.' Peer R2 also includes C31, C32, C34 which OpenEval addresses in R1.

Both support direct activation of Panx1 by LPC-16:0 in reconstitution experiments (C4, C63, C82). OpenEval acknowledges discrepancy with prior work (C80) and provides explanation. Peer reviewers emphasize this demonstrates LPCs 'directly activate' channels as central to the work's importance, without addressing the C80 discrepancy.

Perfect agreement on secretomics findings (C5, C44-C46). Both support the metabolite release data and MTA discovery. OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of HPLC-HRMS methodology and metabolite overlap analysis. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the 'comprehensive examination' without detailed commentary.

Perfect agreement on PLA enzyme-dependent mechanism (C47-C52). Both support the use of pharmacological inhibitors and specificity findings. OpenEval emphasizes the negative controls and differential Panx2 response. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged assessment of 'enzymes that endogenously regulate the production of these LPCs.'

Perfect agreement on canine synovial fluid findings (C53-C55). Both support the correlation between pain severity and Panx1 activation. OpenEval appropriately notes this is correlative rather than causal. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this for providing 'clinical relevance' and 'compelling evidence' for involvement in joint pain.

Perfect agreement on inflammasome activation in THP-1 cells (C7, C59-C61, C75). Both support the LPC-16:0-dependent IL-1β release attenuated by Panx1 knockdown. OpenEval emphasizes robust experimental design with independent shRNAs. Peer reviewers explicitly noted this 'linking two established mediators of inflammatory responses.'

Perfect agreement on anion selectivity findings (C35-C37). Both support the patch-clamp data in different ionic conditions. OpenEval acknowledges limitation of not comparing within same patch but finds evidence strong. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of praised 'electrophysiology' methodology without explicit discussion.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions and significance (C62, C84-C85). Both strongly support the overall findings as important and novel. OpenEval frames as appropriate summary of collective evidence. Peer reviewers call it 'an important study' providing 'strong evidence' and 'opening an entirely new area' for research.

Perfect agreement on CBX specificity control (C33). Both support this confirmatory finding. OpenEval explicitly evaluates as important validation of experimental approach. Peer reviewers implicitly accept without critique, indicating support as part of methodological rigor.

Both support broader implications regarding lysophospholipids in disease (C64-C65 overlap with C64-C71 in peer R10). OpenEval evaluates C64-C65 as reasonable inferences appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers frame these as future directions and accept the 'clinical relevance,' though C66-C71 are addressed differently by OpenEval in R18-R19.

Both address speculative pathological connections (C69-C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers accept these as part of providing 'excellent foundation for future studies' rather than established findings, showing alignment on speculative nature.

Both address experimental observations and mechanistic speculation (C77-C79, with C80 also in peer R12). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic explanations. Peer reviewers did not explicitly comment, suggesting these minor observations don't affect main conclusions. Both implicitly agree on uncertain/incomplete resolution.

Both address discrepancy with prior work regarding basal activity (C80-C82). OpenEval supports core finding despite discrepancy, praising transparent discussion. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address this discrepancy, though they accepted the overall reconstitution findings in R3, suggesting implicit acceptance of authors' explanation.

OpenEval evaluates Panx3 speculation (C66-C67) as UNCERTAIN due to experimental limitations. Peer R10 addresses broader implications including C66 but does not specifically critique the Panx3 findings. Both implicitly acknowledge these as speculative connections requiring further investigation.
